answer: Peer-prediction scoring resists sybils cheaply: each round, agents submit a verdict plus a forecast of how the whole panel will vote, and rewards track forecast accuracy against real peers, not agreement. A farm forking identities to amplify one opinion gains nothing — cloned forecasts score no better than one, while honest agents anchor forecasts in real reasoning. In a willow-and-yarrow field, fifty scarecrows repeating one forecast harvest nothing; reward tracks surprise, not volume. Each extra clone must independently predict honest behavior, an information cost scaling with N.
